existing_specific_text.short_definition: Threatening police, lawyers, HR, or authorities as leverage.
existing_specific_text.expanded_definition: Threatening police, lawyers, HR, or authorities as leverage. Imports institutional force into a personal dispute to compel compliance. As a communication pattern, Legal/Administrative Threats-type behavior in the Institutional & Process category tends to work by using the credibility or procedures of an institution as cover, so a personal or unfair action looks like neutral policy — describing a pattern in the exchange, not a fixed trait in the person.

what_it_is: Threatening police, lawyers, HR, or authorities as leverage.
Imports institutional force into a personal dispute to compel compliance.
Contrasts with a healthier version: using institutions for their actual purpose — safety and rights — not as a club in an argument.
Recognizable by phrasing such as "I'll have my lawyer bury you".
what_it_sounds_like: I'll have my lawyer bury you.
One call to HR and you're finished.
I'll call the police.
You'll be hearing from my lawyer.
I'll have you arrested.
what_it_is_not: Sometimes contacting authorities is the legitimate, correct move; the flag is the threat used as pressure ('unless you…').
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Genuine, appropriate statements of legal intent are a normal part of resolving real disputes.
Accurately informing someone of their real rights isn't the same as threatening them.
common_false_positives: A genuine, appropriate statement of intent to pursue a legitimate legal or institutional process, stated factually rather than as intimidation.
A person accurately informing someone of real rights or consequences, without using it as leverage in an unrelated argument.
A one-time, heated statement in an argument that isn't actually acted on and isn't part of a pattern.
discernment_questions: Is the threatened institutional action proportionate to a real, legitimate grievance, or does it seem designed mainly to intimidate?
Does the threat appear specifically as leverage in an unrelated personal disagreement?
Is this a pattern of invoking institutional force repeatedly, or a one-time, genuine statement of intent?
Would the threatened action, if pursued, actually have a real legal or institutional basis?
less_concerning_if: The threatened action has a genuine legal basis and is stated factually rather than as intimidation in an unrelated dispute.
more_concerning_if: Institutional threats are repeatedly invoked as leverage in personal disagreements, disproportionate to any real basis.

what_it_is_not: Genuine bureaucracy is slow without being aimed at you — the flag is process that accelerates for others and stalls only for the target.

discernment_questions: Is the volume of process proportionate to the actual complexity of the issue?
